We’re introducing StateBench , a benchmark for long-context state tracking —how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as they evolve.
State tracking underlies tasks from reading code, where variables are assigned and reassigned, to following a story as characters physically move around and objects change hands. For example, if a mystery novel states that

en.reason: StateBench tests long-context state tracking across four difficulty levels and finds recurrent and hybrid models generalize farther than transformers, while frontier models fail on harder tasks and longer inputs.

en.title: AI Music Weekly W.A 052
en.summary: This week's AI Music Weekly rounds up recent copyright rules, business shifts and product updates. Korea's Music Copyright Association is exploring a rights-ownership trust for AI music, Spotify plans to launch a compliant AI cover tool, and MiniMax is scaling back its domestic music cloud business. New releases include Suno MCP, a new ElevenLabs sound-effects model and an NI synthesizer. There are also six cutting-edge papers covering audio synthesis, music-score modeling and more — a quick way for music creators and audio developers to catch up on industry trends and practical tools.
en.reason: KOMCA’s 27 October forum targets AI music copyright trust gaps with algorithm-involvement declarations, DAW stems and acoustic screening, alongside Spotify’s compliance AI-cover plans, MiniMax’s China cloud retreat and six frontier papers.

items.title: DeepSeek这次，想把你从AI的监工岗位上解放出来
items.summary: 老金这篇文章把 Super-agent 的机制讲得很直白：Router 像调度员，记住任务关系并分派；Worker 在各自会话里并行执行，耗时操作转后台，独立检查者盯进度和跑偏。它用更多计算换更短、更稳的等待，但公开原型仍偏实验，需配 Harness、独立账号和隔离环境，主动任务先观察、代码先人工合并。

en.title: This time, DeepSeek wants to free you from the job of supervising AI
en.summary: Lao Jin’s article lays out the Super-agent mechanism plainly: the Router acts as a dispatcher, remembering task relationships and assigning work; Workers execute in parallel in their own sessions, time-consuming operations get moved to the background, and independent checkers monitor progress and drift. It trades more compute for shorter, steadier waits, but the public prototype is still experimental and requires a Harness, separate accounts, and isolated environments. Proactive tasks should be observed first, and code should be merged manually first.
en.reason: DeepSeek’s Super-agent design exploration pairs a Router that dispatches tasks with parallel Workers and an independent checker, demoing an agent that adds a font-size setting to the same PR and reports the merge back to group chat.

items.summary:
土豆姐最全 Grok Bot 方法论
土豆姐最全 Grok Bot 方法论
土豆姐最全 Grok Bot 方法论
查看最新动态并加入对话
土豆姐（Lauren Tan，X 账号 @poteto ）是 Grok Bot 客户端的主力工程师，也是全网最会用 Grok Bot 的人之一。她自己的 bot 团队帮她订机票酒店、提醒她吃午饭、盯着 X 上的反馈、管着一群写代码的智能体。她说自己上个月往生产环境提交了两千多个 PR。
我把土豆姐（poteto）所有的演讲、访谈、直播、长文，还有三百多条推文都整合了起来，浓缩整理成一套完整、成体系的 Grok Bot 方法论。
她在每一场演讲、每一次访谈里都会回到同一个词：trust（信任）。
她把用智能体的人分成几档。最低一档是同时开 1 到 5 个对话，每一个都要盯着、不停纠正，人一走开，bot 就做错。她说这一档 最难爬出去 ，因为你不知道该从哪里下手。
卡住的原因只有一个：你还不信任它的产出。不信任的时候，开 100 个 bot 只会得到 100 份要返工的东西。所以要往上爬，靠的不是多开 bot，而是先让一个 bot 做的事情你能信得过。

en.title: Pretty-girl Potato Sister @poteto is one of the most skilled Grok Bot users on the internet.
en.reason: Lauren Tan (@poteto), a lead Grok Bot engineer, says she filed over 2,000 production PRs last month; her integrated talks, interviews, livestreams, essays and 300-plus tweets form a trust ladder that starts with trusting one bot before scaling.

The "intelligent agent" dream from 25 years ago is coming true today — just in a different way

On November 2, MIT Technology Review published a long feature, The Agent Web Has Arrived (https://t.co/rVUmupywZn): today's AI assistants can sort email, compare prices, book restaurant tables and flights, and some are even authorized to access inboxes; websites are also starting to serve content to both humans and AI agents.
en.reason: AI assistants can now sort email, compare prices and book restaurants and flights—some are granted email access—as MIT Technology Review’s November 2 article cites Pew research that AI summaries cut site click-throughs by about 40%.

en.summary:
@TapeAIAgent
I had a long conversation with the TapeAI founder yesterday, and I finally have a clearer picture of the problem this project is trying to solve.

When people talk about AI Agents today, they usually think of Codex, Claude, Doubao, or the various automated trading bots.

They're all smart, and they can call tools, read files, write code, and even operate wallets.

But that's exactly where the problem lies:

As an AI becomes more capable, what do we use to constrain it?

How do we know whose authorization it has?

How much money can it move?

Which addresses must it never send to?

Which contracts must it never approve?

When something goes wrong, who is accountable — the model, the Skill, the developer, or the person who issued the task?

That's the layer TapeAI wants to fill in.

Today's Roundup
This issue has 10 items (4 in-depth commentaries, 6 briefs). Today's main thread is a simultaneous tightening of traceability for AI outputs and the safety boundaries for agents: Anthropic and xAI pushed invisible text watermarks to more models within the same week, while a new study shows that an agent that obtained an email verification code would bypass a user-set spending cap. Another thread is that money for AI infrastructure keeps ramping up: Marvell is acquiring optics maker Lumentum for $115 billion in an all-stock deal, betting on the optical connectivity bottleneck in data centers.
Marvell announced on November 2 an all-stock acquisition of optical components maker Lumentum, with an enterprise value of $115 billion, one of the largest tech deals of 2026, betting that as AI clusters continue to scale, optical connections moving data between chips will become the next bottleneck.
What happened: Under the agreement, each Lumentum share can be exchanged for 4.5 Marvell shares, equivalent to about $1,132 per share, a 23.9% premium to the October 28 closing price (the last trading day before deal rumors emerged).

en.title: This time, DeepSeek wants to free you from the job of supervising AI
en.summary: Lao Jin’s article lays out the Super-agent mechanism plainly: the Router acts as a dispatcher, remembering task relationships and assigning work; Workers execute in parallel in their own sessions, time-consuming operations get moved to the background, and independent checkers monitor progress and drift. It trades more compute for shorter, steadier waits, but the public prototype is still experimental and requires a Harness, separate accounts, and isolated environments. Proactive tasks should be observed first, and code should be merged manually first.
en.reason: DeepSeek’s Super-agent design exploration pairs a Router that dispatches tasks with parallel Workers and an independent checker, demoing an agent that adds a font-size setting to the same PR and reports the merge back to group chat.

土豆姐（Lauren Tan，X 账号 @poteto ）是 Grok Bot 客户端的主力工程师，也是全网最会用 Grok Bot 的人之一。她自己的 bot 团队帮她订机票酒店、提醒她吃午饭、盯着 X 上的反馈、管着一群写代码的智能体。她说自己上个月往生产环境提交了两千多个 PR。
我把土豆姐（poteto）所有的演讲、访谈、直播、长文，还有三百多条推文都整合了起来，浓缩整理成一套完整、成体系的 Grok Bot 方法论。
她在每一场演讲、每一次访谈里都会回到同一个词：trust（信任）。
她把用智能体的人分成几档。最低一档是同时开 1 到 5 个对话，每一个都要盯着、不停纠正，人一走开，bot 就做错。她说这一档 最难爬出去 ，因为你不知道该从哪里下手。
卡住的原因只有一个：你还不信任它的产出。不信任的时候，开 100 个 bot 只会得到 100 份要返工的东西。所以要往上爬，靠的不是多开 bot，而是先让一个 bot 做的事情你能信得过。

en.title: Pretty-girl Potato Sister @poteto is one of the most skilled Grok Bot users on the internet.
en.reason: Lauren Tan (@poteto), a lead Grok Bot engineer, says she filed over 2,000 production PRs last month; her integrated talks, interviews, livestreams, essays and 300-plus tweets form a trust ladder that starts with trusting one bot before scaling.

en.title: @TapeAIAgent I had a long talk with TapeAI's founder yesterday, and I now have a much clearer picture of the problem this project is trying to solve.
en.summary:
@TapeAIAgent
I had a long conversation with the TapeAI founder yesterday, and I finally have a clearer picture of the problem this project is trying to solve.

When people talk about AI Agents today, they usually think of Codex, Claude, Doubao, or the various automated trading bots.

They're all smart, and they can call tools, read files, write code, and even operate wallets.

But that's exactly where the problem lies:

As an AI becomes more capable, what do we use to constrain it?

How do we know whose authorization it has?

How much money can it move?

Which addresses must it never send to?

Which contracts must it never approve?

When something goes wrong, who is accountable — the model, the Skill, the developer, or the person who issued the task?

That's the layer TapeAI wants to fill in.

en.reason: TapeAI is building a constraint layer for AI agents such as Codex and Claude that can operate wallets, addressing who authorized an agent, how much it may spend, which addresses and contracts are off-limits, and whether blame for errors falls on the model, Skill, developer or task issuer.

Today's Roundup
This issue has 10 items (4 in-depth commentaries, 6 briefs). Today's main thread is a simultaneous tightening of traceability for AI outputs and the safety boundaries for agents: Anthropic and xAI pushed invisible text watermarks to more models within the same week, while a new study shows that an agent that obtained an email verification code would bypass a user-set spending cap. Another thread is that money for AI infrastructure keeps ramping up: Marvell is acquiring optics maker Lumentum for $115 billion in an all-stock deal, betting on the optical connectivity bottleneck in data centers.
Marvell announced on November 2 an all-stock acquisition of optical components maker Lumentum, with an enterprise value of $115 billion, one of the largest tech deals of 2026, betting that as AI clusters continue to scale, optical connections moving data between chips will become the next bottleneck.
What happened: Under the agreement, each Lumentum share can be exchanged for 4.5 Marvell shares, equivalent to about $1,132 per share, a 23.9% premium to the October 28 closing price (the last trading day before deal rumors emerged).
en.reason: Anthropic expands its invisible text watermark on November 3 to Mythos 5, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, but a customer email says changing temperature, top_p or top_k removes it from the latter two.
